From 65782b2db7321d5f97c16718c4c7f6c7205a56be Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Davide Caratti <dcaratti@redhat.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 17:24:36 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net/sched: cls_fw: fix NULL dereference of "old" filters
 before change()

Like pointed out by Sashiko [1], since commit ed76f5edccc9 ("net: sched:
protect filter_chain list with filter_chain_lock mutex") TC filters are
added to a shared block and published to datapath before their ->change()
function is called. This is a problem for cls_fw: an invalid filter
created with the "old" method can still classify some packets before it
is destroyed by the validation logic added by Xiang.
Therefore, insisting with repeated runs of the following script:

 # ip link add dev crash0 type dummy
 # ip link set dev crash0 up
 # mausezahn  crash0 -c 100000 -P 10 \
 > -A 4.3.2.1 -B 1.2.3.4 -t udp "dp=1234" -q &
 # sleep 1
 # tc qdisc add dev crash0 egress_block 1 clsact
 # tc filter add block 1 protocol ip prio 1 matchall \
 > action skbedit mark 65536 continue
 # tc filter add block 1 protocol ip prio 2 fw
 # ip link del dev crash0

diff --git a/net/sched/cls_fw.c b/net/sched/cls_fw.c
index 23884ef8b80c..646a730dca93 100644
--- a/net/sched/cls_fw.c
+++ b/net/sched/cls_fw.c
@@ -74,9 +74,13 @@ TC_INDIRECT_SCOPE int fw_classify(struct sk_buff *skb,
 			}
 		}
 	} else {
-		struct Qdisc *q = tcf_block_q(tp->chain->block);
+		struct Qdisc *q;
 
 		/* Old method: classify the packet using its skb mark. */
+		if (tcf_block_shared(tp->chain->block))
+			return -1;
+
+		q = tcf_block_q(tp->chain->block);
 		if (id && (TC_H_MAJ(id) == 0 ||
 			   !(TC_H_MAJ(id ^ q->handle)))) {
 			res->classid = id;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file, `net/sched/cls_fw.c`, to fix a NULL pointer dereference in the `fw_classify()` function when using "old-style" classification on filters installed in a shared block.

**Modifications:**
- In the `else` branch of `fw_classify()`, which handles the legacy (old-style) classification method, a check for `tcf_block_shared(tp->chain->block)` is added before retrieving the Qdisc pointer via `tcf_block_q()`. If the block is shared, the function returns `-1` immediately (indicating no match) instead of proceeding to dereference the Qdisc pointer. This prevents access to a potentially NULL `q` when the filter’s block is shared, as the block may not have an associated Qdisc in that context.

**Relationships:**
- The change is directly related to the root cause described in the commit message: after commit `ed76f5edccc9`, filters are added and published to datapath before their `->change()` function runs. For cls_fw, this means an "old-style" filter (one that classifies by the skb mark) can be active while its configuration is incomplete (e.g., `q` may be NULL), causing crashes. The added guard skips the forced old-style classification on shared blocks, preventing the NULL dereference and the preceding `WARN_ON()` that occurs due to the short-lived invalid filter.

Here is the root cause:
Filters are published to datapath before their ->change() function completes, allowing old-style cls_fw filters on shared blocks to access a NULL Qdisc pointer in fw_classify().

Here is the patch:
 
 TC_INDIRECT_SCOPE int fw_classify(struct sk_buff *skb,
 				  const struct tcf_proto *tp,
 				  struct tcf_result *res)
 {
 	struct fw_head *head = rcu_dereference_bh(tp->root);
 	struct fw_filter *f;
 	int r;
 	u32 id = skb->mark;
 
 	if (head != NULL) {
 		id &= head->mask;
 
 		for (f = rcu_dereference_bh(head->ht[fw_hash(id)]); f;
 		     f = rcu_dereference_bh(f->next)) {
 			if (f->id == id) {
 				*res = f->res;
 				if (!tcf_match_indev(skb, f->ifindex))
 					continue;
 				r = tcf_exts_exec(skb, &f->exts, res);
 				if (r < 0)
 					continue;
 
 				return r;
 			}
 		}
 	} else {
-		struct Qdisc *q = tcf_block_q(tp->chain->block);
+		struct Qdisc *q;
 
 		/* Old method: classify the packet using its skb mark. */
+		if (tcf_block_shared(tp->chain->block))
+			return -1;
+
+		q = tcf_block_q(tp->chain->block);
 		if (id && (TC_H_MAJ(id) == 0 ||
 			   !(TC_H_MAJ(id ^ q->handle)))) {
 			res->classid = id;
 			res->class = 0;
 			return 0;
 		}
 	}
 
 	return -1;
 }
